signals.name: storedBytesRead
signals.quantity: total bytes returned by readStored(byte[],int,int) summed across all calls in one execution
signals.reset: V1Counters.reset() called at the start of V1Guidance.getInput()

plans.retention: Keep inputs where storedBytesRead exceeds the current best in the corpus. While signal is flat (storedBytesRead == 0), retain inputs that (a) have grown toward 32 bytes and (b) start with PK\x03\x04 (valid LFH signature). Corpus sorted by storedBytesRead descending; parents selected from top-10.
mutation: Byte-level: random byte flip, random byte overwrite, random byte insertion, random byte deletion
Repetition [R45a]: copy a region of the input and repeat it k times to fill toward MAX_INPUT_SIZE; can duplicate an entire LFH+data section to create multi-entry archives
Dictionary [R45b]: tokens from the attack path source — LFH_SIG, CFH_SIG, EOCD_SIG, STORED/DEFLATED methods, UTF-8 leads, max 32-bit size
Size-field targeting: mutate bytes at LFH offsets 18-25 (compressed size, uncompressed size) to explore large declared sizes
No encoder needed [R45c]: raw ZIP bytes with no compression/checksum layer to satisfy

signals.name: decompressedBytes
signals.quantity: total bytes returned by BZip2CompressorInputStream#read(byte[],int,int) summed across all calls in one execution
signals.reset: PkgRisk1Counters.reset() called at the start of PkgRisk1Guidance.getInput()

plans.retention: Keep inputs where decompressedBytes exceeds the current best or corpus is small (<20). ALWAYS retain inputs that are longer than the current longest encoded input [R46], regardless of signal value, to ensure input_growth toward 3100 bytes. Corpus cap 100; evict lowest signal then shortest.
mutation: Grow bomb (30%): double the uniform (zeros) plaintext size from 1KB to 64MB, encoding through BZip2CompressorOutputStream [R45c]; cached per size, so each size is encoded only once; at 64MB the single entry is ~110 bytes encoded but decompresses to 67,108,864 bytes (matching the scale series structure)

Grow diverse (30%/60%): encode a fresh plaintext of increasing size (starting 500 bytes, +200-500 each step) of random bytes through BZip2CompressorOutputStream [R45c]; random data compresses at ~1:1, so a 2800-byte plaintext produces a ~3100-byte encoded input, satisfying input_bytes=3100 for input_growth [R46]
Mutate corpus (20%): select a corpus entry and flip 1-3 bytes in the bzip2 data area (after the 31-byte ZIP LFH header) for exploration
Reuse bomb (20%): resubmit the current best bomb entry for consistent high-signal measurements

Well-formed encoding [R45c]: all inputs are single ZIP entries encoded through BZip2CompressorOutputStream from the vulnerable jar on the classpath, with correct CRC32, compressed/uncompressed sizes, and method 12
